title: Sprint 95 prefetch / kernel exchange and KV-batch sketch
body:
Context / why this note: quick mid-sprint sketch to capture the ad-hoc sync (04/17) where we tried to reconcile kernel handshake changes with the new KV-batch coalescer prototype. This is intentionally rough — goal is to capture decisions, immediate experiments, and handoff items for next shift.

Attendees: Aisha (note), Marco, Lina, Evan, Priya, Sam (oncall drop-in)

High-level takeaway:
- We have two small patches that conflict at runtime: kernel-handshake v3 (low-latency path selection) and kv-coalescer v2 (aggressive prefetch + grouping). Together they sometimes over-allocate KV slots and cause transient mem-pressure + small latency spikes for 0.5% of requests.
- Action: run a controlled canary where kernel-handshake uses a conservative slot estimator for 24 hours; throttle coalescer growth until we have telemetry to correlate request traces to slot allocation.

Agenda items covered:
1) Reproduce failure mode (short summary)
   - Symptoms: tail latency bump seen in 03:30–04:00 UTC window for a single host pool. Traces show kernel handshake escalating batch-size estimation then coalescer prefetch filling KV capacity -> short GC-like stall (~20–40ms).
   - Repro steps (local/nightly): replay sampled traffic from 2029-04-15 03:30 UTC through the micro-batcher harness with both patches enabled. Ticket: jira/INF-2421.

2) Root cause hypothesis
   - Kernel-handshake now interpolates sequence-length distribution and recommends larger micro-batches for amortized kernel launch cost.
   - Coalescer prefetch policy was tuned for higher throughput and assumes elastic KV headroom; the handshake estimation removed slack and coalescer growth hits shadows causing backpressure.

3) Short-term mitigations
   - Canary config: add kernel-handshake conservative estimator flag (handshake.estimate_bias = -0.25) for 1 host in the canary pool.
   - Coalescer safety: add soft cap for number of prefetched KV entries per request (coalescer.max_prefetch_per_req = 8).
   - Rollout plan: canary for 24h, then check tail pct (p99.9) and mem-pressure gauges.

4) Experiment matrix we agreed to run
   - A: baseline (no changes) — 24h sample, control host.
   - B: handshake conservative estimator only — measure p95/p99/p99.9 token latency, kv-cache hit/miss delta.
   - C: coalescer soft cap only — measure throughput and tail latency.
   - D: both conservative estimator + soft cap — verify stability and cost impact.
   - Metrics to collect: kernel-launch time, per-token latency, kv-cache occupancy, eviction rate, GC stalls, CPU/GPU utilization, request traces for failed/slow requests.

5) Longer-term design notes and ideas (brainstorm)
   - Adaptive headroom: maintain a moving quantile of observed KV occupancy that coalescer consults before aggressive prefetch. Prefer 95th percentile over fixed caps.
   - Backpressure-aware handshake: handshake estimator should be KV-aware — if occupancy > threshold X, bias estimator downward to avoid overcommit.
   - Prefetch prioritization: older requests get prefetch priority; new concurrent requests get sampled prefetches until headroom frees.
   - Admission control hook: allow the serving runtime to temporarily reject speculative prefetch for low-priority requests when cluster-level headroom < Y.

6) Action items (who/what/when)
   - Aisha: create the canary config and kick off canary job; link logs to jira/INF-2421. Due: 2029-04-18 EOD.
   - Marco: implement handshake.estimate_bias flag and wire to runtime config system; add unit tests. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1387. Due: 2029-04-19.
   - Lina: implement coalescer.max_prefetch_per_req soft cap and add metric coalescer.prefetch_denied_count. Quick patch, prioritize for canary. Due: 2029-04-18 AM.
   - Evan: extend tracing sampler to capture KV occupancy snapshots at request start/end (trace annotation: kv.occupancy_start / kv.occupancy_end). Due: 2029-04-20.
   - Priya: run the experiment matrix and record results in the experiment sheet (confluence/serving-runtime/prefetch-ideas). Start: 2029-04-19.
   - Sam (oncall): watch the canary and escalate on p99.9 > baseline + 25ms or mem-pressure > 85%.

7) Observability / dashboards to create/update
   - New panel: per-host KV occupancy heatmap (1m resolution). Owner: Lina.
   - New alert: kv-cache-eviction-rate spike (>3x baseline sustained for 2m). Owner: SRE team.
   - Trace grouping: add group filters for (kernel-handshake-version, coalescer-version) to speed correlation. Owner: Evan.

8) Open questions / risks
   - Will conservative estimator degrade throughput materially? We expect small throughput loss; need cost delta estimate before wide rollout.
   - If we cap per-request prefetch too low, QPS-sensitive workloads might see higher token-cost due to missed amortizations. Need to measure token-per-request cost change.
   - Cross-pool variance: some host pools with larger memory can sustain current coalescer settings; gating logic must be pool-aware.

9) Notes to self / rough TODOs (non-blocking)
   - Add a small simulation that replays arrival patterns and simulates handshake + prefetch interplay (quick prototype in py). Good for hypothesizing.
   - Check prior notes from Nov 2027 on "prefetch-backpressure-playbook" for heuristics we tested earlier. Might salvage a tuning knob.

10) Handoff / next sync
   - Next ad-hoc check-in: 2029-04-19 09:30 PT (15 min) to share initial canary telemetry.
   - If canary looks good, plan staged rollout with 10% -> 50% -> 100% host pool progression.

Appendix: quick snippet (for the ops runbook)
- Canary config flags:
  - handshake.estimate_bias = -0.25
  - coalescer.max_prefetch_per_req = 8
  - coalescer.prefetch_denied_metric = true

- Quick replay command (dev box):
  ./tools/replay_traffic --sample-hostpool hostpool-canary --start 2029-04-15T03:30:00Z --end 2029-04-15T04:00:00Z --apply-patches handshake-v3,coalescer-v2

End of note. Any additions/corrections drop into this doc; I'll fold into jira/INF-2421 before the canary starts.
